topic: Namespace and Scope Resolution in C++
explanation: In C++, namespaces and scope resolution operators (::) are used to organize code and specify the context in which identifiers (such as variables, functions, or classes) are defined. This mechanism allows disambiguation of names, especially in large projects with multiple modules, classes, and nested scopes. The scope resolution operator (::) explicitly indicates the namespace or class scope where a particular identifier resides, enabling precise access to members and avoiding name conflicts. Understanding how scope resolution searches through various nested and enclosing scopes is fundamental for correctly referencing variables and functions in complex codebases.
code_example: // Local variable 'i' is not declared here
int i = 42; // Global variable in namespace M::N
int i = 100; // Global variable in namespace M
int i = 200; // Global variable in global scope
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how the scope resolution operator (::) is used to access variables in different nested scopes. Inside the function M::N::X::f(), the code explicitly references the global variable 'i' with ::i, as well as static class members X::i and B::i, showing how scope resolution clarifies which variable is being accessed. The example also illustrates the hierarchy of scopes from local to global, emphasizing how C++ searches through these scopes to resolve identifiers. This demonstrates the importance of scope resolution in managing name visibility and avoiding ambiguity in complex C++ programs.
